land.text: the Huguenot-held coast of Saintonge and Aunis around La Rochelle: Cliopatria's 1622 polygon plus La Rochelle

predecessors.note: A rebel enclave on royal land. The pages name the south-west and Languedoc strongholds only in general ('66 villes de surete', Montpellier, 'mainly in southwestern France'); only the coastal polygon is drawn.

land.text: the Huguenot enclave's remnant polygon, and La Rochelle, taken in October 1628

successors.note: La Rochelle surrendered unconditionally on 28 October 1628; under the Peace of Alais the Huguenots 'lost their territorial, political, and military rights but kept the religious freedom of the Edict of Nantes' (Siege page); the Huguenots page dates the Edict of Ales to 1629.

capitals.name: La Rochelle
capitals.note: The stronghold of the rebellion: 'La Rochelle fired the first shots at royal troops' on 10 September 1627 and surrendered on 28 October 1628. The pages do not call it a capital. Coordinates are the gazetteer's place La Rochelle.

correction.text: the first year of the rising, drawn with the 1622 polygon as stand-in, plus La Rochelle

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1622. 'Louis re-established Catholicism in Bearn, which led to an uprising by Henri de Rohan and Soubise' in 1621 (Siege page); 'Three small civil wars ... between 1621 and 1629' (Huguenots page). The extent in 1621 is not described by either page; the 1622 polygon is a stand-in.

correction.text: Cliopatria's polygon on the Charente-Maritime coast with La Rochelle, the Huguenot stronghold, added

keyframe_review.note: 1622-1628, 1,916 km2 (6 cells, bbox -1.24 to -0.73 E, 45.50 to 46.15 N): a coastal polygon in Saintonge south of La Rochelle, which lies just outside it (46.17 N). The Siege page's whole story is La Rochelle (siege 10 September 1627 to 28 October 1628; 'the population of La Rochelle decreased from 27,000 to 5,000'), so the city is added. The Treaty of Montpellier (October 1622) ended the first revolt 'in stalemate'. No page gives an area.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 715 km2 (2 cells), holding 1629 only: the Huguenots lose their territorial rights with the Edict of Ales of 1629, and Cliopatria's 1630-1631 years belong to the crown

keyframe_review.note: 1629-1631 in Cliopatria. The Huguenots page: the rebellions 'led to the abolition of their political and military privileges'; 'Protestant rule in Montpellier had already ended before the Edict of Ales (1629)'. The Siege page: under the Peace of Alais the Huguenots 'lost their territorial, political, and military rights'. The remnant polygon after La Rochelle's fall is not described by either page.

region.text: the Huguenot coast of Saintonge and Aunis with La Rochelle

ledger.note: 1621: the Huguenots rise against the crown. 'Louis re-established Catholicism in Bearn, which led to an uprising by Henri de Rohan and Soubise' (Siege page); the Huguenots page: 'Three small civil wars, the Huguenot rebellions, broke out mainly in southwestern France between 1621 and 1629.' The year is the pages'; the land is Cliopatria's polygon plus La Rochelle (the pages give no outline). Capital La Rochelle.

region.text: La Rochelle and its surroundings, besieged by the royal army from 10 September 1627

ledger.note: 10 September 1627: the siege of La Rochelle begins. 'La Rochelle fired the first shots at royal troops at Fort Louis, starting the siege', after royal forces under Charles of Angouleme began surrounding the city in August; Buckingham had landed about 6,000 men on the Ile de Re in June 1627.

28 October 1628: La Rochelle surrenders. 'The city surrendered. Surrender was unconditional'; the population fell from 27,000 to 5,000 during the siege; the English relief fleet of September 1628 had withdrawn.
28 October 1628: the crown takes La Rochelle, the Huguenots' main stronghold. The surrounding polygon stays with the rebels until the 1629 Edict of Ales.

region.text: the remnant of the Huguenot enclave after La Rochelle, with its territorial rights abolished

ledger.note: 1629: the Edict of Ales ends the Huguenots' territorial and military privileges. 'The Huguenot rebellions led to the abolition of their political and military privileges'; 'Edict of Ales (1629)' (Huguenots page); the Siege page: they 'lost their territorial, political, and military rights but kept the religious freedom of the Edict of Nantes'. Neither page gives the month. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1631.

wars.name: Huguenot rebellions
wars.outcome: Three small civil wars in south-western France; the Treaty of Montpellier ended the first in stalemate in October 1622 (Siege page), the crown took La Rochelle in October 1628 and the Huguenots lost their territorial, political and military privileges in 1629.
wars.note: The Huguenots page also records the royal siege of Montpellier in 1622 ('fortifications dismantled, a royal citadel built'); Montpellier and the other south-western strongholds lie outside Cliopatria's polygon and are not drawn.

wars.name: Siege of La Rochelle
wars.outcome: The royal army, with a 1,400 m seawall and 12 km of entrenchments, starved the city out: unconditional surrender on 28 October 1628. English relief by Buckingham on the Ile de Re (June 1627) and by Lindsey's fleet (September 1628) failed.
wars.note: The Siege page calls the English intervention the Anglo-French War of 1627.

certainty.note: A rebel enclave without a boundary: neither page outlines the Huguenot-held land, and the polygon is Cliopatria's. The siege lines round La Rochelle (12 km of entrenchments) are the only measured frontier.

sources.title: Huguenots
sources.note: The Edict of Nantes (66 villes de surete), the rebellions of 1621-1629, Montpellier 1622, the Edict of Ales 1629; no La Rochelle chronology.

sources.title: Siege of La Rochelle
sources.note: The 1621 rising, Treaty of Montpellier 1622, Ile de Re June 1627, siege 10 September 1627 to 28 October 1628, the terms of the Peace of Alais; no date for the Peace.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Huguenots' (1622-1631, 1,916 and 715 km2) is a coastal polygon south of La Rochelle, not the Huguenot strongholds of the south-west and Languedoc (Montauban, Montpellier, the 66 villes de surete of 1598), which the pages name only in general. The dossier runs 1621-1629 (new 1621 keyframe; the row ends with the Edict of Ales, not 1631) and adds La Rochelle to the 1622 polygon. The Huguenots page says nothing on La Rochelle and the Siege page nothing on the Edict of Grace or the date of the Peace of Alais (June 1629 is not on either page). Page budget (1-2) spent: Huguenots and Siege of La Rochelle. Needs a dossier from the eu-10-x additions batch if the map wants the south-western and Languedoc strongholds: 'Huguenot strongholds / rebellion of the Duke of Rohan 1621-1629' (rebel). The Ile de Re was held by royal troops at Saint-Martin-de-Re in 1627 (Siege page, not explicit) and is not drawn. No area figure on either page.
